messages:
Priya (CS): Quick weekly pulse for HelioRetail — focused on error-rate breakdown and top failing endpoints. Overall request error rate this week: 2.3% (+0.8ppt WoW). High-level split: 5xx = 0.92 (≈40% of errors), Timeouts = 0.80 (≈35%), Rate-limits/429 = 0.58 (≈25%).

Priya (CS): Top failing endpoints by error count (last 7d):
1) POST /v1/chat/stream — majority 5xx (502/504), 48% of total 5xx. spikes correlate with large multi-turn sessions.
2) POST /v1/generate — elevated p95 latency and timeouts during longer prompts (seq > 1024).
3) POST /v1/embeddings/batch — 429s concentrated between 11:00-13:00 PST, bursty client behavior.
4) GET /v1/status/model — intermittent 500s coming from model-agent health checks.
5) POST /v1/ingest — small # of 5xx tied to backend qdepth on gpu-pool-7.

Priya (CS): Recent changelog: HelioRetail was on model-x-v1 until last Tue canary (model-x-v2) for higher throughput. Canary shows higher p99 compute and some cache miss regressions. Also observed increased retry traffic from client SDK when requests error -> exacerbates rate limits. Customer CSM flagged potential renewal concern if SLOs don't improve.

Jordan (SRE): looked through traces — pattern: tensor-host-03 returning 502s when request token_count > ~2000. Backend queue depth + CPU hot spots visible on gpu-pool-7 cluster. Query I ran: `service:api status:502 path:/v1/chat/stream | stats count() by host` — tensor-host-03 accounts for ~60% of those 502s.

Jordan (SRE): Hypothesis: model-x-v2 kernel path isn't handling long-context continuous batching well -> latency/timeouts -> upstream returns 502/504. Recommend immediate rollback for HelioRetail canary and enable fallback to model-x-v1 for new sessions. Also throttle retry behavior at gateway for 5xx to avoid retry storms. :eyes:

Alex (Platform): I can bump HelioRetail dedicated pool scale and tighten gateway retry for that account only. Will push a scale + rate-limit override to the dedicated group and monitor. Planning to add +4 instances to dedicated/helio-pool; applying now.

deploy-bot: Started scale action: dedicated/helio-pool +4 instances. Change-id: cp-helio-2026-03-21-01. ETA ~3m.

Ania (ENG): Agree with rollback + scaling. Also propose we add a server-side pre-check to early-fail requests that exceed a safe token threshold to avoid spending cycles on doomed requests. Suggested config snippet to enforce for HelioRetail (temporary):
```json
{"max_tokens_per_request":4096, "timeout_ms":45000, "retry_policy": "no-retries-on-5xx-backoff"}
```
This returns a 4xx with guidance rather than letting client retry and hit 429s.

Jordan (SRE): I'll open an incident timeline and attach spike graph + top trace samples. If rollback doesn't reduce 5xx within 15m, we proceed to full canary rollback and route traffic to v1 for that customer.

Priya (CS): Action items summary:
- Jordan: rollback canary for HelioRetail if 5xx rate doesn't drop to baseline in next 15m; open incident doc + attach traces.
- Alex: scale dedicated/helio-pool +4 (in flight) and add account-level retry override.
- Ania: PR to enforce token cap + better 4xx with user guidance; include client SDK guidance to reduce aggressive retries.
- Priya: schedule HelioRetail sync (Wed 10:00 PT) and offer temporary credits + status update.

Priya (CS): I'll send a short customer note once we confirm stabilization. Thanks all — please react with :thumbsup: when you've completed your items so I can close loop with the CSM.

Alex (Platform): scale completed, monitoring p95/p99 now. posted new autoscale target to infra. :white_check_mark:

Jordan (SRE): traces attached in incident doc — 3 red sample traces uploaded. 5xx down ~65% after scaling, still watching timeouts.

Ania (ENG): opened PR #3421 with token cap + early-fail behavior, marking for review.

Priya (CS): Marking this thread as the weekly error-breakout for HelioRetail. I'll export this summary to the customer deck and include next steps.

Priya (CS): (closing note) If anyone sees renewed 429 bursts, ping me directly so I can coordinate credits/communication with the customer.
